registry_rule: Existing Object Registry remains the only contract-selection registry; this is a traceability record, not a new database or competing current-state index.

references.application: One caller-owned transaction; typed exactTx owner reads; actor parent fences absent Social roots; no nested commit/foreign SQL/semantic read effects.
invariants: One command owns one transaction; nested owner ports accept caller transaction and never commit independently.

Before first canonical mutation, command-specific typed plans close every possible transactional canonical effect and required synchronization identity. Include indirect EXP/energy, overflow/Mail, immediate objectives, references and receipt/fact/obligation source rows.

Plan known keys or an explicit conservative superset. If a locked read discovers another key, expand before mutation and reacquire/retry in global order. Never acquire an out-of-order lock after mutation.

Post-commit notification, transport writing and River worker execution are delivery work, not extra gameplay-owner locks. Their durable source rows/obligations participate only according to their actual transactional ownership.
No universal effect-graph engine is mandated. Command-specific typed planners and existing global lock-rank registry suffice.
Each canonical row has exactly one owner; cross-owner code calls narrow typed ports. Missing-row creation fences a stable namespace/parent synchronization key.
Semantic receipt, immutable economic ledger, response payload and durable obligation remain distinct. Failed delivery after commit never authorizes repeat settlement.
acceptance: Rollback leaves no partial debit/grant/objective/obligation
Composite indirect effect uses global lock order
Concurrent missing owner rows create one identity
No nested transaction or direct foreign-owner SQL

references.application: Database response observation is separate from durable gameplay decision time; no new scheduler/reset/clock authority.
invariants: Generation owns explicit occurrence identity, scope, time policy and lifecycle. Wall-clock recomputation is not the identity of an already accepted operation.
Jobs are at-least-once wakeups. Owner tables/obligations remain truth; job uniqueness is not economic idempotency. Reconciliation recreates lost delivery from durable obligations.

Facts have stable identity, owner aggregate revision, schema and causal operation reference. Consumers record deduplication and ordering policy; ordering is per relevant aggregate, not a promised global order.

Immediate objective effects participate in preplanned transaction locks. Deferred projections declare revision/watermark and read-your-write behavior. Realtime notifications cannot be the only durable evidence.
ActivityDirectory aggregates qualified owner providers and availability. It never authorizes spending/rewards or turns an unqualified capability on.
Shared scope retains participant character/logical-server identity. Cross-server namespaces require explicit owner keys and arbitration, not widening a character key.

Client timers/scene entry are not expiry or settlement authority. Authoritative admission and owner reconciliation enforce validity; jobs only wake durable owner obligations. Distinguish validity cutoff from physical deletion and retained receipt/tombstone history.

Shared packet claims require an occurrence owner and atomic arbitration over remaining allocation and recipient claims; notifications only project committed facts. Exact scope, supply, expiry and allocation policy must be researched before activation.
Work Place / TREASURE528-540 must satisfy PASS465_WORKPLACE_TIME_CONTRACT.json; clock infrastructure and inactive projection do not establish feature completion.

AUDIT-PROFILE-05: Work Place recovery/spend uses its canonical resource/refresh facts and existing typed effect/transaction plan. UI timers and scheduler wakeups do not define server completion.
AUDIT-PROFILE-05: Record remainder, at-cap, elapsed interval and backwards-time handling as qualified policy before affected schema/command freeze; no silent policy guessed from display code.

references.application: Private attempted output and stable operation selection anchor; unknownCOMMIT not replay permission; stock read does not identify successor mutation intent.
invariants: Guarantee at-most-once settlement for a known semantic operation. Do not equate this with perfect identification of every identical nonce-less stock request.
Transport write success means bytes accepted by transport, not application consumption. Rename such state to TRANSPORT_WRITE_RECORDED; it cannot by itself advance a consumptive replay lane.

Classify each family: intrinsic one-shot key, provider receipt key, explicit source nonce, or ambiguous repeatable parameters. Strong keys use semantic receipts; parameter hashes alone are not universal operation identity.

For ambiguous repeatable consumptive families default to fail-closed ambiguity after an unresolved operation. Reconnect, lease expiry and receipt age alone do not prove new intent. A family may adopt an explicit bounded compatibility policy only with documented residual duplicate/false-replay tradeoff and W2 acceptance; no universal no-double-charge claim.
Retention preserves receipt/tombstone meaning across restore. Expiry must not silently reopen a previously settled one-shot entitlement. Response payloads never retain raw credentials.
No private nonce or modified-client acknowledgment may be required of an unmodified stock client.

Practice SAVE identifies actor without candidate revision. Internal revision fencing prevents stale internal writes, but cannot perfectly identify whether a delayed nonce-less SAVE intended an older or newly replaced draft. Require family-specific conservative/compatibility policy, as with repeated paid requests; no private client nonce or perfect stale-intent guarantee.

references.application: No schema change; exact candidate/native restart/dump-restore proof required; research probes do not satisfy implementation gate.
invariants: Every owner added now declares schema version, forward migration/backfill, source mapping, identity/tombstone retention and rollback/roll-forward boundary. Do not defer owner data semantics to I13.

Restore creates/records history epoch and reconciles external payments/receipts before reopening writes. Retain semantic operation identity across restore; never pretend recovered queue delivery proves external settlement.
Preserve Pass425 RPO/RTO policy as acceptance targets, not achieved measurements. Backup success is not restore proof.

I12 is global integration hardening, not first concurrency test. R7 proves repaired foundation on real PostgreSQL/River; each later owner carries scoped DB concurrency/recovery proof. W2 remains comprehensive real stock-client/restore/migration/load acceptance after I14.

I14 runs available checks and enumerates unavailable checks with exact evidence needs. Replace literally every test possible with a versioned risk/requirement inventory; missing evidence cannot become PASS.

I15 reconciles each required capability, acceptance row and outstanding unknown against actual evidence. No release with unresolved required feature dependencies; deliberately inactive features must be source-compatible and explicitly approved in release scope.

references.application: Additive narrow owner ports with consumers, compatibility, lock/effect and proof records; no generic registry/repository/bus.
invariants: Supersede absolute prohibition on future interface edits. Prefer additive narrow typed ports; permit evidence-backed versioned interface evolution when an actual new responsibility requires it.

A change record names source contradiction/new capability, owning package, consumers, data migration, compatibility adapter, lock/effect changes and acceptance evidence. Deprecate old version only after consumer migration.
No opaque map, reflection registry, generic foreign-table repository or bypass SQL solely to avoid changing a port.
Keep modular monolith and PostgreSQL transaction boundary. Separate processes are justified only by isolation/operational need, such as battle resolver; no new universal event bus or ledger owner.
Modularity is a reviewable ownership/dependency property, not a guarantee that unforeseen discoveries never change foundations.
